newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe targets break-even results in H2.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe targets break-even results in H2.

text.p: CompuServe Inc said Wednesday it expects to continue narrowing its losses in the coming quarters, with a goal of achieving break-even results sometime in the second half of fiscal 1998.

The online services company reported Wednesday that it lost $17.9 million or $0.19 per share after consolidation charges totalling $5.8 million after taxes, or $0.06 per share in its fiscal fourth quarter ended April 30.
Excluding the charge, CompuServe lost $0.13 per share, trimming the $0.15 per share it lost in its third quarter. The company gave itself mixed reviews for the performance.
"Our fourth-quarter results were encouraging in some respects and disappointing in others," Frank Salizzoni, CompuServe chairman and acting chief executive said in a statement.

"Overall, we made progress toward our goal of stabilizing earnings and returning CompuServe to profitability," he said. "We expect further improvement in earnings and cash flows, our goal being to reach or exceed the breakeven point in earnings sometime in the second half of the current 1998 fiscal year."

CompuServe's timetable for stemming its losses has broad ramifications for the company, particularly because it would allow 80 percent owner H&R Block Inc to carry through on plans to separate from CompuServe.
"H&R Block has said that one criteria for a spin-off is a return to profitability," Herb Kahn, executive vice president of corporate operations at CompuServe said in an interview.
H&R Block continues to consider other methods of divesting CompuServe, including an outright sale.
Talks regarding a possible sale, disclosed by H&R Block in early April, remain underway, said Kahn, but he declined to offer further details.
